query: dependency inversion principle interfaces abstractions architecture
title: System Design: Dependency Inversion Principle | Baeldung on Computer Science
snippet: The Dependency Inversion Principle states that high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions. The principle introduces an interface abstraction between higher-level and lower-level software components to remove the dependencies between them.
claim: Dependency inversion requires high-level modules to depend on abstractions rather than low-level implementations.

title: Capability-Based Architecture: A Practical Guide to Portability, Isolation, and AI-Readiness - DEV Community
snippet: Capabilities are defined with explicit manifests, actions with typed schemas, events with documented contracts, and mounting configurations that declare where everything lives. This structural clarity enables better isolation and multi-channel deployment while supporting AI integration.
claim: Capability-based architecture isolates concerns through explicit interface definitions and typed schemas.

query: hexagonal architecture ports adapters external dependencies
title: Hexagonal architecture pattern - AWS Prescriptive Guidance
snippet: Hexagonal Architecture, also known as Ports and Adapters Architecture, is a software design approach that separates the core business logic from external systems like databases, APIs, and user interfaces. This architecture addresses the issue of coupling by creating loosely coupled architectures where application components can be tested independently.
claim: Hexagonal architecture isolates core logic from external dependencies through ports and adapters.

query: clean architecture core imports interfaces not implementations
title: Implementing clean architecture solutions: A practical example | Red Hat Developer
snippet: No implementations should reside in the core layer, only interfaces for injection. The domain layer depends on abstractions (repository interfaces) rather than concrete implementations, which adheres to the dependency inversion principle.
claim: Clean architecture requires the core layer to depend only on interfaces, never concrete implementations.

query: service interface boundaries software design patterns
title: The "Service Interface" Pattern | Microsoft Learn
snippet: Interfaces called Boundaries allow calls across architectural layers, where one side makes calls and expects agreed-upon responses, while the other side receives calls and returns responses, with both sides usually not knowing who is on the other side and simply acting upon requests and responses.
claim: Service interface boundaries decouple layers by defining contracts that both sides must respect.

title: What is Abstraction Layer? 2026 Overview | Rubrik
snippet: The concept of an abstraction layer simplifies interactions with complex systems by hiding intricate details behind a straightforward interface, and by separating the internal workings of a system from its external operations, abstraction layers enable flexibility, modularity, and ease of use.
claim: Abstraction layers decouple internal implementations from external interfaces, enabling flexibility and modularity.
